items.title: Global stocks rally as investors shrug off U.S. tariffs and AI jitters to 'fish for bargains'
items.take: With U.S. cash markets closed for Thanksgiving, global investors are fishing for bargains: Europe is rebounding after Wednesday's decline as the new tariff round reads less bad than feared. The open question is whether Wall Street's late recovery can hold once trading resumes.

items.title: US stock markets closed for Thanksgiving, Wall Street prepares for shortened Black Friday session
items.take: NYSE and Nasdaq are dark today and reopen Friday for a half-day session ending at 1:00 PM Eastern, typically among the year's thinnest volume. Light trading can exaggerate moves, so Friday's tape is directionally suspect until full attendance returns next week.

items.title: General Market Analysis: a mixed Thanksgiving-eve session
items.take: Wednesday split down the middle: technology kept sliding while the Dow edged higher, and stocks recovered a large chunk of their earlier losses by the close. Tellingly, yields and the dollar fell even with a December hike all but locked in, a sign positioning, not data, is steering.

items.title: GDP revised up to 4.3% annual pace, the fastest in three years
items.take: Third-quarter GDP was revised to 4.3% from an initial 3.4%, the fastest growth in three years, which complicates the sell-off's story of a weakening economy. A resilient economy plus sticky inflation is exactly the combination that keeps a December 9 rate hike on the menu.

items.title: After the holiday: jobs data takes the wheel next week
items.take: The calendar empties for the holiday, then fills fast: next week's reports culminate in the December 4 nonfarm payrolls reading, the Fed's last big data point before the December 9 decision. With a hike priced near-certain, the jobs number now sets the tone for 2027 policy.
